title: Mixed-workload scheduler prototype (short/long prompt-aware scheduling) — initiative
creator: Talia Benson
content:
## Initiative overview

We see elevated p95 (and occasional p99) tail latency under mixed prompt-length distributions (short chat prompts interleaved with long-context prompts / long-prefill). Current continuous batching + batch selection tends to allow long-prefill requests to dominate selection and create head-of-line blocking for latency-sensitive short prompts.

This initiative prototypes a short/long prompt-aware scheduling policy (two-queue or class-based scheduling) that prioritizes short prompts while preserving throughput and guaranteeing progress for long prompts (aging + skew caps + token budgets).

Primary owners:
- Scheduling: Sofia Ivanova (EM), Lena Fischer (TL), Marcus Reed, Omar El-Sayed, Julian Moore
- Kernels/runtime interactions: Hiro Tanaka (EM), Grace Kim, Yuki Sato
- SRE/Observability: Sean Gallagher, Allison Grant, Rafael Mendes, Aisha Bello

Non-goals (prototype phase):
- Multi-tenant QoS productization (customer-configurable tiers beyond internal knobs)
- Large admission control redesign (minimal coupling to existing backpressure only)


## Success criteria / how we’ll measure

### Target outcomes
1) Tail latency improvement under mixed workloads
- Reduce user-visible generation p95 latency by **>= 20%** on the 80/20 short/long synthetic mix (short = typical chat prompts; long = long-context/prefill-heavy) vs baseline scheduler.
- Reduce TTFT p95 by **>= 15%** under the long-spike scenario (bursts of long-prefill) without regressions in steady short-only workloads.

2) Throughput and cost guardrails
- No more than **5% throughput regression** (tokens/sec) at iso-quality in benchmark-lab mixed scenarios.
- No increase > **3%** in GPU memory pressure attributable to scheduler behavior (e.g., pathological KV cache churn driven by scheduling).

3) Fairness / starvation prevention
- Long class must make forward progress: no long-request starvation under sustained short traffic.
- Starvation counter must remain below threshold in perf-canary + canary pools (exact alert thresholds defined by SRE).

4) Operational readiness
- Feature-flagged and parameterized rollout with safe bounds.
- Dashboards & alerting for per-class queue depth, time-in-queue, dispatch share, starvation counters, and per-class p50/p95.
- Runbook with rollback triggers aligned to Hosted API tail-latency SLO guardrails.

### Metrics to report (minimum)
- p50/p95/p99 for end-to-end latency and TTFT
- Queue time distribution (overall + per-class)
- Prefill latency and decode latency breakdown
- Throughput (tokens/sec) and GPU utilization
- Per-class dispatch share and token budget overruns


## Proposed approach (prototype)

- Request classification:
  - Classify requests as SHORT vs LONG based on prompt/context length and/or predicted prefill cost.
  - Keep classification logic simple and configurable (thresholds per pool / per model).

- Two-queue dispatch policy:
  - Maintain separate queues for short and long.
  - Bias selection toward short while enforcing a minimum service share for long.
  - Add aging and max-skew guardrails to prevent starvation.

- Prefill/decode separation hooks:
  - Avoid long-prefill dominating batch construction when mixed with short decode.
  - Ensure kernel selection remains stable (avoid thrashing when mixing sequence lengths).

- Token budget guardrails:
  - Per-iteration token budgets per class to cap tail amplification.
  - Instrument budget overruns with counters + debug logs.


## Timeline (hypothetical, used for planning)

Phase 0 (1–2 wks): analysis + design review + ADR
- Analyze anonymized prompt-length distributions; propose thresholds and sensitivity.
- Confluence design + ADR review with kernels + SRE.

Phase 1 (2–4 wks): implement prototype behind flag + instrumentation
- Implement classification, two-queue dispatch, aging/starvation prevention.
- Add per-class metrics and tracing.

Phase 2 (2–3 wks): benchmarking and parameter iteration
- Add benchmark-lab mixed scenarios; run parameter sweeps.
- Perf-canary nightly job + regression alerts.

Phase 3 (1–2 wks): limited production canary + decision
- Canary in one region and subset of Dedicated pools.
- Monitor SLO guardrails; rollback on triggers.
- Decision meeting: graduate / iterate / stop.


## Deliverables

Engineering deliverables:
- Scheduler implementation behind flag, with safe defaults and config plumbing
- Tests: unit/regression + at least one mixed-workload load test scenario
- Metrics: per-class queue depth, time-in-queue, starvation counters, dispatch share, p95 by class

Operational deliverables:
- Dashboard spec + initial dashboard
- Rollout runbook and rollback procedure
- Canary plan with owners and schedule

Decision artifacts:
- ADR documenting why short/long prompt-aware scheduling was chosen vs SRPT approximation vs admission-control-only
- Benchmark methodology + results summary


## Risks / open questions

- Kernel selection instability when mixing sequence lengths:
  - Risk: perf regressions from kernel thrash; mitigation: prefill/decode separation + kernel team review.

- Fairness and multi-tenant implications:
  - Risk: starving long requests or violating implicit fairness expectations; mitigation: aging + min-share + max skew; keep behind flag.

- KV cache behavior:
  - Risk: scheduling changes increase cache eviction spikes; mitigation: add cache eviction / memory pressure counters to dashboards and check during canary.

- Parameter tuning complexity:
  - Risk: too many knobs; mitigation: constrain to a small set with safe bounds, provide recommended defaults per SKU.


## Linked work / sub-issues

- ENG-2421 — Collect and summarize production prompt-length distribution
- ENG-2426 — Design review: mixed workload scheduler
- ENG-2432 — Implement short/long request classification
- ENG-2438 — Implement two-queue scheduling with aging
- ENG-2441 — Add per-class scheduler metrics and traces
- ENG-2449 — Add mixed workload benchmarks to benchmark-lab
- ENG-2456 — Integrate mixed-workload scenarios into perf-canary
- ENG-2463 — SRE review: rollout guardrails
- ENG-2470 — Release plan: enable scheduler prototype in us-east canary

Product alignment dependency:
- PM-612 — Define success metrics for tail latency improvement (Hosted vs Dedicated)


## Comms plan

- Weekly 30-min sync: #eng-runtime (Scheduling + Kernels + SRE) during Phases 1–3
- Design review in #architecture after ADR draft
- Canary comms in #eng-releases with explicit on-point + rollback authority


## Updates (internal)

2025-11-22 (Talia Benson)
- Created initiative; aligned with Sofia/Lena on scope and initial milestone breakdown. Waiting on PM-612 to finalize success metric wording for Hosted vs Dedicated.

2025-12-03 (Sofia Ivanova)
- Phase 0 underway: trace analysis in progress; initial threshold candidates for SHORT/LONG drafted. Kernel team flagged potential kernel selection thrash risk; asked that prefill/decode separation be part of Phase 1, not a follow-up.

2025-12-12 (Lena Fischer)
- Draft dispatch policy proposal: two-queue with min long-share + aging. Added explicit requirement for starvation regression test and metric. Next step: schedule design review (ENG-2426) and lock prototype knobs (keep it to ~3–5 config fields with bounds).


## Acceptance criteria (initiative-level)

This initiative is considered complete when:
- Prototype can be enabled/disabled via feature flag and safely ramped via config
- Benchmarks show target p95 improvements on mixed scenarios with throughput regression <= 5%
- Starvation prevention verified via tests + perf-canary + canary monitoring
- Dashboards + alerts + runbook exist and are used in a limited canary
- Decision made (graduate / iterate / stop) with written results summary and next steps
